details.amebic-colitis: One colon-wall cutaway with a characteristic flask-shaped ulcer whose submucosal spread exceeds its narrow mucosal opening, simple readable anatomy.
details.amebic-liver-abscess: One correct gross liver cutaway with a localized rounded abscess containing sober brown-red opaque contents, non-graphic, no dish or drain automatically inserted.
details.cryptosporidiosis: A simple intestinal villus cutaway with small organisms attached at brush-border surface and blunted villus contour, no decorative dots outside tissue.
details.cyclosporiasis: One coherent small-intestinal mucosal cutaway with localized villous injury and modest lumen fluid, no produce/fruit background.
details.cystoisosporiasis: One small-intestinal villus epithelial cutaway with a few intracellular parasite structures fully within cells and modest villous blunting.
details.cutaneous-leishmaniasis: One forearm skin crop with a single chronic shallow ulcer with raised indurated border, no insect prop.
details.visceral-leishmaniasis: One correct isolated enlarged spleen with a small limited internal cutaway conveying reticuloendothelial involvement, no whole-body multi-organ collage.
details.chagas-disease: One correct gross heart cutaway with modest dilated ventricular geometry representing chronic cardiomyopathy, no unrelated giant esophagus beside it.
details.african-trypanosomiasis: A natural ordinary adult bust with drowsy expression and modest cervical lymph-node swelling, no impossible sleep pose or flying insect.
details.strongyloidiasis: A simple skin crop with a short fast-moving serpiginous urticarial track on lower abdomen/upper thigh region, no giant adult worm outside body.
details.strongyloides-hyperinfection: One correct simple lung cutaway containing a few small larval forms and patchy inflammation, not a whole life-cycle scene.
details.ascariasis: One correct small-bowel cutaway with a few coherent slender adult worms inside the lumen, no worm passing through intact bowel into arbitrary organs.
details.enterobiasis: A sober small perianal skin/tissue schematic with one small slender pinworm at surface, nonsexual and no whole nude child.
details.trichuriasis: One correct colonic mucosa cutaway with one whipworm whose slender anterior portion is embedded in mucosa and thicker posterior lies in lumen.
details.hookworm-infection: One small-intestinal mucosal cutaway with a single attached hookworm at surface and a modest localized blood-feeding site, non-graphic.
details.schistosomiasis: One anatomically coherent liver/portal tissue cutaway showing modest periportal fibrosis and a few embedded eggs; do not combine all species' organ complications.
details.clonorchiasis: Correct simple liver and biliary tree cutaway with a few small leaf-shaped adult flukes INSIDE enlarged bile ducts, no worms on outer liver surface.
details.paragonimiasis: One correct lung cutaway with a localized fluke-containing cyst and small adjacent inflammatory change; no giant crab prop.
details.fascioliasis: One accurate liver cutaway with a limited serpiginous migratory tract within parenchyma and one leaf-like fluke near a bile duct.
details.taeniasis: One simple intestinal lumen cutaway with a short attached tapeworm scolex and a few connected proglottids, no cysticercus in brain for adult intestinal disease.
details.neurocysticercosis: One correct brain cutaway with a few round cystic lesions, one with a tiny contained eccentric scolex; no giant adult tapeworm on brain surface.
details.echinococcosis: One accurate gross liver cutaway with a single encapsulated hydatid cyst and a few daughter cysts entirely within it, no free outside bubbles.
details.toxocariasis: One simple correct liver tissue cutaway with a small localized inflammatory migratory larval focus, no adult worms or fecal eggs in human gut.
details.trichinellosis: One accurate skeletal-muscle bundle cutaway with a few coiled larvae inside oval nurse-cell capsules, no whole animal meat prop.
details.anisakiasis: One correct stomach cutaway with a SINGLE slender cream larva attached to gastric mucosa and local inflammation, not a mature tapeworm.
details.scabies: One natural hand/wrist skin crop with five fingers and a short narrow burrow in an interdigital web space, no floating giant mite outside skin.
details.cutaneous-larva-migrans: One natural foot/lower-leg crop with a single clearly serpiginous raised red track on skin. Exactly five toes if foot visible; no arbitrary dotted trail outside body.
details.lymphatic-filariasis: One naturally aligned lower leg/foot with chronic lymphatic edema and thickened skin, five toes, no impossible ankle or obligatory grotesque deformity.
details.onchocerciasis: One forearm skin crop with a modest subcutaneous nodule and local chronic skin change, no fly prop or obligatory destroyed eyeball.
details.loiasis: One correct natural eye crop with a single slender adult worm visible beneath conjunctiva, intact singular iris/pupil, no worm emerging from pupil.
details.dracunculiasis: One natural lower-leg crop with a small blister and a thin continuous cream worm gradually emerging from that one opening, no detached winding body.
details.primary-amebic-meningoencephalitis: One correct simple brain-and-meningeal cutaway with intense localized meningoencephalitic inflammation, no drinking-water pathway arrow.
details.granulomatous-amebic-encephalitis: One correct brain gross cutaway with a few modest granulomatous focal parenchymal lesions, no amoeba face or extra brain lobes.
details.balantidiasis: One simple correct colon mucosal cutaway with a localized ulcer and one oval ciliated organism confined to the luminal tissue interface, no whole life cycle.

categories.gastrointestinal: Use one compact anatomically plausible bowel wall/colon cutaway showing the localized mucosal pattern from the notes. If necessary an ordinary abdomen crop behind the organ, arms/hands outside frame. Do not draw fluids or stool floating outside the patient.
categories.hepatobiliary: One correct gross liver with a modest attached biliary outline if required. Use localized inflammatory/red tissue and notes' clinically stated change; chronic hepatitis is not automatically end-stage cirrhosis.
categories.eye: One medically correct eye or eye cutaway, with a single round iris/pupil at front and localized lesion at correct ocular layer. Do not use multiple pupils, broken eyelid joints, impossible eye sockets or skull decoration.
categories.sti: Use a sober anatomically correct local tissue/organ cutaway appropriate to the supplied disease. Avoid explicit nude patient portraits. A syphilis chancre can be a small skin cutaway rather than sexualized anatomy; no stigma or romance props.
categories.bacterial: Select the most specific ordinary symptom/site explicitly described in DB clinical core, and depict one simple body-part crop or accurate gross organ. No pathogen mascot substituted for the disease.
categories.viral: Select the main clinical organ/site or characteristic visible skin pattern explicitly described in DB. A clothed natural patient crop is suitable for fever/rash; no fanciful virus-as-monster symbolism.
categories.fungal: Depict the actual clinical affected organ or skin lesion from DB notes, rather than a fungal organism alone. Gross organ anatomy stays simple and correct.
categories.parasitic: Depict the clinical affected organ/site with one characteristic lesion from DB notes. A parasite is drawn only if it is actually in that anatomical site. Avoid life-cycle infographics.
